title: Victorian barrier geometry: height, non-climbable zones and gaps
audience: Pool barrier installers, inspectors and service workers checking pool barriers in Victoria. Altering a permanent barrier is building work needing a permit in Victoria. The rules are Victorian.
learningOutcomes: Measure barrier height from the finished ground level and compare it with the Victorian figure for internal and boundary barriers.
Explain non-climbable zones and check their reach against the note.
Check mesh, gaps, steps, ledges and intersecting barriers against the note.

instruction.heading: Measuring height and the non-climbable zones
instruction.body: Victorian rule (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, Version 3, 26 September 2023). Height is measured at right angles to the finished ground level (FGL). SP 02 numbers five non-climbable zones (NCZ 1 to NCZ 5), and this lesson calls them Zone 1 to Zone 5. Zone 1 is a 900 mm vertical plane on the outside of an internal barrier. Zone 2 is a quadrant with a 900 mm radius from the top of Zone 1. Zone 3 is a quadrant with a 900 mm radius from the top of the barrier, on the outside. Zone 4 covers vertical openings of 10 to 100 mm, 900 mm high and 300 mm deep, on the inside. Zone 5 applies to boundary barriers. An internal barrier of 1800 mm or more needs no non-climbable zone. The barrier standard is AS 1926.1-2012, cited by name only.

instruction.heading: Boundary fences used as barriers
instruction.body: A boundary fence serving as the pool barrier must be at least 1800 mm high on the inside. Zone 5 is a quadrant with a 900 mm radius down from the top of the inside face. Owners and occupiers must maintain the barrier and adjacent vegetation, and plants that could help a child climb are not permitted within the non-climbable zones.

instruction.heading: Steps, ledges and crossing barriers
instruction.body: Steps or level changes that abut a barrier must be set back at least 500 mm from it. This set-back does not apply to boundary barriers. Projections and indentations more than 10 mm deep should not be climbable. Where a lower internal barrier meets a boundary fence, the top rail decides the outcome. If the top rail is 50 mm wide or less and meets the boundary barrier at 45 to 135 degrees, the junction meets the rule. Otherwise, the lower barrier must reach 1800 mm and extend at least 900 mm from the intersection.

instruction.heading: Mesh panels, openings and bottom gaps
instruction.body: A non-boundary mesh barrier must be at least 1200 mm high where its openings are 13 mm or less, and at least 1800 mm where openings are over 13 mm and up to 100 mm. Openings wider than 100 mm are not allowed. Under a 25 kg weight applied at any point on the top, the barrier must stay at 1200 mm or more. Openings are measured horizontally across the widest part. For mesh or perforated barriers, the gap at the base must stay within 100 mm when a 100 N vertical lift force is applied.

instruction.heading: Glass barriers
instruction.body: SP 02 says glass must comply with AS 1288. High-risk glass must be Grade A safety glazing of the minimum thickness that AS 1288 prescribes. AS 1288 is cited by name only, and its wording was not read for this lesson.

procedure: Establish the finished ground level on both sides of the barrier, and take the height from it.
Decide whether the barrier is internal or a boundary fence, and apply the matching height and zone figure.
Check each zone, and confirm no climbable projection or object sits inside Zone 1.
With mesh or perforated panels, record the width of each opening and the space at the base.
Record the measurements, the rule applied and the result, and report any shortfall in writing.

workedExamples.situation: An internal barrier around a pool stands 1100 mm high and meets an existing 1800 mm boundary fence at a right angle. The internal barrier's top rail is 70 mm wide.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Does the internal barrier comply at the junction?
workedExamples.reasoning: The internal barrier is under 1800 mm, so the zones apply. The top rail is wider than 50 mm, so the lower barrier has to rise to 1800 mm across a run of at least 900 mm beyond the junction. As it stands the arrangement does not comply. Record the finding and report it to the builder, since any change is building work needing a permit.

equipmentAndPpe: Ruler or gauge for mesh openings
Calibrated spring scale for force checks, where a tester is trained

commonErrors.error: Measuring height from a raised deck or step rather than from the ground surface.
commonErrors.prevention: Measure from the finished ground level, not from a raised deck or step.

commonErrors.error: Using mesh with 20 mm openings at a 1200 mm height.
commonErrors.prevention: Check opening width and height together against the mesh rule.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a flat ledge inside Zone 1.
commonErrors.prevention: Check for ledges and recesses in Zone 1 at every inspection.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A barrier a child can scale, or a gap underneath, can give a small child access to the water. Report any gap or climbable feature as a drowning hazard.
Altering or repairing a permanent barrier is building work that needs a permit in Victoria. Registration may also apply. This lesson grants neither.
Figures are Victorian (VBA Building Practice Note SP 02, 2023). The named standards, the 2012 edition of AS 1926.1 and AS 1288, were not read.

qualityStandard: Barrier height is recorded from the ground surface, with the measurement point stated.
Non-climbable zones are checked against the rule for the barrier type.
Mesh opening, bottom gap and load results are recorded for each section tested.
documentationEvidence: Barrier measurement record with height, ground reference, zone check and result
Mesh and gap record with opening widths, bottom gap and load check
summary: Measure barrier height from the finished ground level; internal barriers under 1800 mm need non-climbable zones.
A boundary fence needs at least 1800 mm on the pool side, with a zone 900 mm down.
Mesh has limits on opening width and height, a bottom gap limit, and must keep its height under load.

officialReferences.title: Pool safety barriers
officialReferences.covers: Victorian Building Authority consumer page, read through a summary tool. States that pools and spas that can hold water deeper than 300 mm need a compliant barrier to restrict access by children under five; gates must be self-latching and self-closing; barriers must comply with AS1926.1-2012; a new outdoor pool or spa area must not be directly accessible from a building. Names Checklists 1 to 3 and the Building Regulations 2018. Does not state barrier height, non-climbable zone or gap dimensions, and does not name Practice Note 05-2018. The current status of AS 1926.1 is not yet confirmed.

officialReferences.title: Building Practice Note SP 02, Swimming pool barriers and other requirements (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3
officialReferences.covers: Building Practice Note SP 02 (Victorian Building Authority), Version 3, published 26 September 2023. Its superseded list names Version 2.0 (20 April 2023) and Version 1.0 (June 2021) only, and the document shows no review or under-review status. It sets barrier height measured from finished ground level, non-climbable zones NCZ 1 to 5 with 900 mm planes and radii, and mesh heights of 1200 mm (apertures up to 13 mm) and 1800 mm (apertures over 13 mm to 100 mm). It does not set out a general inspection or sign-off process for barriers.
